note: Drafted rules whose refute-first verification did not run (session limit, 2026-09-03); not generated into tables until verified.

rules.fork: Two-electron integral notation: Mulliken vs Dirac vs antisymmetrized
rules.branch: Mulliken (chemists') notation (pq|rs): the bracket pairs p–q and r–s, i.e. the two indices of each electron sit together
rules.rival: Dirac (physicists') ⟨pq|rs⟩, which pairs p–r and q–s; and the antisymmetrized ⟨pq||rs⟩ = ⟨pq|rs⟩ − ⟨pq|sr⟩
rules.magnitude: J ↔ K swap; a hidden difference of terms
rules.meaning: round brackets with a single bar and two indices per side: Mulliken pairing, so the first pair belongs to electron 1 and J = (pp|qq)
rules.census: §5 round-3 additions, row 'Two-electron integral notation: Mulliken vs Dirac vs antisymmetrized' — Detection: 'bracket glyph + bar count'
rules.notes: The third negative is the GW inner product (h|h), a genuine homograph excluded by requiring two index tokens on each side. The census's fallback — where NO bracket is printed (g_pqrs, the Helgaker/Koch CC school), read the operator's index pairing e_pqrs — is not machine-checkable from a bracket glyph and is not drafted here.

rules.branch: B is defined against the spectral energy density per unit frequency ρ_ν: A₂₁ = (8πhν³/c³)B₂₁
rules.rival: the ρ_ω basis A = (ħω³/π²c³)B, the ρ_ν̃ (per wavenumber) basis, and the mean-intensity J̄_ν basis A = (8πhν³/c²)B
rules.magnitude: up to ~1.5×10¹⁰ between two quantities both printed as 'B₂₁'
rules.meaning: the A–B bridge carries 8πhν³/c³: B multiplies the spectral energy density per unit frequency ρ_ν, in J⁻¹ m³ s⁻²
rules.census: §5 round-3 additions, row 'Einstein B-coefficient basis (ρ_ν/ρ_ω/ρ_ν̃/J̄_ν)' — Detection: 'which A–B relation is printed; B's units'
rules.notes: The Planck spectral energy density u_ν = (8πhν³/c³)/(e^{hν/kT}−1) prints the identical ratio and is the live homograph; the pattern is therefore anchored on an adjacent Einstein-coefficient symbol A_·/B_· (uppercase, subscripted) rather than on the ratio alone, and u_ν is carried as a negative. Does not separate the ρ_ν̃ (per-wavenumber) branch from ρ_ν when the paper prints neither bridge.

rules.fork: Mixing amplitude: sin²2θ vs sin²θ vs |U_αi|²; the θ₂₃ octant
rules.branch: the double-angle amplitude sin²2θ_ij is what is printed and tabulated
rules.rival: sin²θ_ij (the PDG global-fit form), or the matrix element |U_αi|²
rules.magnitude: sin²2θ₁₃ = 0.0851 ↔ sin²θ₁₃ = 0.02174 (×3.91); sin²2θ₂₃ = 0.9787 ↔ 0.573 or 0.427 (×1.34 plus the octant flip)
rules.meaning: The 2 sits inside the sine: the tabulated number is sin²2θ, up to 3.91 times the sin²θ a global fit reports.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Neutrino row 2 ('Mixing amplitude: sin²2θ vs sin²θ vs |U_αi|²; the θ₂₃ octant (corrected)'), Detection column 'token form; the magnitude prior decides'
rules.notes: Only the token leg is a rule. The census's magnitude prior ('0.085 is sin²2θ, 0.022 is sin²θ') is a numeric adjudicator, not a printed form, and the θ₂₃ octant is not resolved by either — sin²2θ₂₃ maps to two sin²θ₂₃ values.

rules.fork: Δm² labels ₃₁ / ₃₂ / ₃ℓ / ee / μμ / atm, plus the ordering sign
rules.rival: Δm²₃₂, the ordering-dependent Δm²₃ℓ, or the effective Δm²_ee / Δm²_μμ
rules.magnitude: 2.95% between ₃₁ and ₃₂; ee 0.90% below; μμ 2.39% below and δ-dependent — not a fixed relabel; ×(−1) between orderings
rules.meaning: The subscript is 31: the tabulated splitting is m₃²−m₁², 2.95% away from the Δm²₃₂ a neighbouring table prints.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Neutrino row 1 ('Δm² labels ₃₁ / ₃₂ / ₃ℓ / ee / μμ / atm, plus the ordering sign'), Detection column 'the subscript token'
rules.notes: The ordering-sign leg is not in the pattern: the footnote 'ℓ = 1 for NO, 2 for IO' is prose and belongs to a Δm²₃ℓ rule. Unverified: the 2.95% / 0.90% / 2.39% offsets are quoted from the census, not recomputed here.

rules.fork: Majorana-phase halving: e^(iα₂₁/2) vs e^(iα₂) in the diagonal phase matrix
rules.branch: halved exponent: the diagonal Majorana matrix carries e^{iα₂₁/2}
rules.rival: unhalved e^{iα₂}, where the same numerical α means twice the physical phase
rules.magnitude: factor 2 in the phase; IO at m₃ = 0: m_ββ 48.35 vs 18.35 meV (×2.635); a mis-halved 'α = π' gives 36.57
rules.meaning: The exponent is halved: α₂₁ is twice the phase that multiplies the mass eigenstate, so m_ββ folds cos(α₂₁) not cos(2α₂).
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Neutrino row 4 ('Majorana-phase halving: e^(iα₂₁/2) vs e^(iα₂) …'), Detection column 'count the ½ in the printed exponent; symbol names correlate but never decide'
rules.notes: The census warns the symbol name (α₂₁ vs α₂) correlates but never decides, so the pattern keys on the printed /2 and admits either name. Not covered: a paper that prints the phases only inside m_ββ.

rules.fork: Fidelity F vs F² (Uhlmann/Nielsen–Chuang vs Jozsa/Wilde)
rules.branch: squared (Jozsa/Wilde) fidelity: the outer square is printed on the trace of the nested root
rules.rival: the Uhlmann/Nielsen–Chuang root fidelity with no outer square
rules.magnitude: infidelities differ by exactly 2 near unity — a quoted '99.9%' is 1.0 or 2.0×10⁻³
rules.meaning: The outer square is printed: F is the Jozsa fidelity, and 1−F is twice the infidelity of the root convention.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Quantum information row 2 ('Fidelity F vs F² (Uhlmann/Nielsen–Chuang vs Jozsa/Wilde)'), Detection column 'the outer square in the printed definition'
rules.notes: F = |⟨ψ|φ⟩|² is a NEGATIVE on purpose: for pure states both conventions agree that the squared overlap is the squared fidelity, so it discriminates nothing. The census's second leg (d_B² = 2(1−F) vs 2(1−√F)) is not in the pattern — it is a second equation and inverts the naming, so it needs its own rule. The normalizer deletes \mathrm{Tr} and \operatorname{tr} entirely, so the pattern cannot key on the trace symbol.

rules.fork: Trace-norm ½ conventions: trace distance, negativity, diamond distance
rules.branch: the ½ is printed: D(ρ,σ) = ½‖ρ−σ‖₁, maximum 1
rules.rival: the bare trace norm ‖ρ−σ‖₁ with no ½, maximum 2
rules.magnitude: exactly ×2 each and independent across the three — a chained diamond → trace → failure argument can be off by 4
rules.meaning: The ½ is printed on the trace norm: D is normalized to 1 at perfect distinguishability, half the bare-norm number.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Quantum information row 4 ('Trace-norm ½ conventions: trace distance, negativity, diamond distance'), Detection column 'the printed definition and the stated maximum (1 vs 2)'
rules.notes: Only the trace-distance leg. The census says the three ½'s are INDEPENDENT, so this rule must not be read as fixing negativity or the diamond norm; the negativity form is listed as a negative for exactly that reason.

rules.fork: Depolarizing channel: uniform-mixing p vs per-Pauli p
rules.magnitude: exactly 4/3 for a qubit, 15/16 for two qubits; a '1% threshold' is 0.75% in the other convention
rules.meaning: The p is divided by three across the Pauli terms: p is the per-Pauli error probability, 4/3 of the uniform-mixing p.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Quantum information row 6 ('Depolarizing channel: uniform-mixing p vs per-Pauli p'), Detection column "'p I/d' vs '(p/3)Σ_P PρP'"
rules.notes: Qubit-specific: the 3 is d²−1 at d = 2. A two-qubit per-Pauli channel prints p/15 and this rule stays silent — correctly, since the census's 15/16 leg is a different denominator. The Qiskit-vs-Cirq leg is a code-identity tell and is not in the pattern.

rules.fork: Entropy/information log base (bits vs nats vs dits) as a unit, not a factor
rules.branch: base 2: the entropy is counted in bits (shannons)
rules.magnitude: 1 nat = 1.442695 bits; k_B ln 2 = 9.5699×10⁻²⁴ J/K; Landauer 17.92 meV at 300 K against k_BT = 25.85 meV
rules.meaning: The logarithm carries base 2: the entropy is in bits, 1.442695 times the same quantity in nats.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Quantum information row 1 ('Entropy/information log base (bits vs nats vs dits) as a unit, not a factor') and Thermodynamics row 4 ('Entropy log base against the k_B = 1 generator'), Detection columns 'the base printed on the log (many write bare log)' and "log₂/lg/'bits'/'shannon'"
rules.notes: n = log₂ d is a negative: a dimension count is not an entropy convention. The census's 'lg' spelling and the bare-'log' majority case are deliberately not matched — a bare log is negative evidence, per §6.5b, never a default to nats.

rules.fork: Thermodynamic sign block: the first-law work sign and its siblings
rules.branch: W is work done BY the system: dU = δQ − δW (Clausius / physics-engine convention)
rules.rival: W done ON the system: dU = δQ + δW (IUPAC / chemistry)
rules.magnitude: exact flip on W, η, W_ext, W_diss; RT ln 2 = 1.729 kJ/mol quoted ±; every tabulated E° (Zn²⁺/Zn ∓0.76 V)
rules.tex: dU = \delta Q - \delta W \qquad (W \text{ done } \textit{by}\text{ the system})
rules.meaning: The work term enters with a minus sign: W is the work done by the system, and every reported W, η and E° flips against the IUPAC convention.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Thermodynamics row 1 ('Thermodynamic sign block: the first-law work sign and its siblings (corrected)'), Detection column 'the printed first law; dU = TdS − pdV is identical either way — only a named W shows it'
rules.notes: dU = TdS − pdV is a negative because the census says so explicitly: it is identical in both conventions. The normalizer deletes \mathrm{d}, so the leading differential is optional in the pattern and the rule keys on the Q − W structure alone.

rules.branch: Stratonovich: the midpoint product ∘ is printed on the noise increment
rules.rival: Itô (plain product, no ∘) or Hänggi–Klimontovich (anti-Itô / post-point)
rules.magnitude: p_ss ∝ D(x)^(α−1): uniform, D^(−1/2), D^(−1) — a 3× diffusivity spread gives stationary densities 1 : 1.73 : 3
rules.meaning: The ∘ marks a midpoint product: the SDE is Stratonovich, and its drift differs from the Itô one by ½ b ∂_x b.
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Thermodynamics row 2 ('Stochastic-calculus prescription (Itô / Stratonovich / Hänggi–Klimontovich)'), Detection column 'the ∘ on the noise integral; a drift term in ∂_xD — its presence IS the prescription'
rules.notes: Guarded against the degree symbol (^\circ and ^{\circ}) and against bare function composition by requiring a noise differential after the ∘. Not covered: papers writing \mathrm{d}W, since the normalizer deletes \mathrm{d} and the residual '∘ W' is indistinguishable from composition. The census's second leg — a ∂_xD drift term — is a structural check, not a token, and is deliberately absent.

rules.fork: Level-reference registry by medium, era and discipline (20 μPa / 1 μPa / 1 μbar; ISO 1683; dBu–dBV)
rules.branch: airborne acoustics: the 0 dB reference is 20 μPa
rules.rival: underwater 1 μPa (+26.02 dB), the pre-SI 1 μbar = 0.1 Pa (+100.0 dB exactly), or a power reference such as 1 pW
rules.magnitude: 26.02 dB (20 μPa → 1 μPa); 100.0 dB exactly (μbar → μPa); 61.5 dB air↔water
rules.meaning: The stated reference is 20 μPa: the level is an airborne sound-pressure level, 26.02 dB below the same pressure quoted re 1 μPa.
positives: sound pressure level in dB re 20 µPa
the threshold is 0 dB re 20 muPa at 1 kHz
negatives: the source level is 183 dB re 1 µPa²·s
antenna gain 12 dBi, power 30 dBm re 1 mW
the figure shows 20 μPa of pressure
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Acoustics row 2 ('Level-reference registry by medium, era and discipline (20 μPa / 1 μPa / 1 μbar; ISO 1683; dBu–dBV)'), Detection column "'re 0.0002 dyn/cm²', 're 1 pW'; dBm with a stated or unstated Ω"; the surrounding row 1 supplies the 're'/'ref.' token itself
rules.notes: Only the air branch. The 1 μbar / 0.0002 dyn·cm⁻² era branch and the dBu/dBV/dBm electrical branches are separate rules; the dyn/cm² form is carried here as a negative so this rule never claims it. Papers that write the reference only in a figure axis label are out of reach of a prose pattern.

rules.fork: Amplitude statistic (rms / 0-peak / peak-to-peak / average) as a mandatory tag
rules.branch: peak-to-peak: the quoted amplitude spans trough to crest
rules.rival: rms (÷2√2 for a sinusoid), 0-peak (÷2), or rectified average
rules.magnitude: sinusoid: peak/rms = √2 (3.010 dB), pk-pk/rms = 2√2 (9.031 dB) — one or two ISO 20816 severity zones
rules.meaning: The amplitude tag is peak-to-peak: for a sinusoid the number is 2√2 times the rms value the severity standard grades.
positives: the airgun signature is quoted pk-pk
displacement amplitude, peak to peak, 25 μm
rules.census: §5 round-4 five-lens table, Acoustics row 3 ('Amplitude statistic (rms / 0-peak / peak-to-peak / average) as a mandatory tag'), Detection column "rms/0-pk/pk-pk/'crest factor'; a bare mm/s must warn, never default"
rules.notes: Asserts only the pk-pk branch; the census's real deliverable is that a bare mm/s must warn, which is a lint, not a rule. 'p-p' and bare 'pp' are excluded as too ambiguous. Guarded against 'peak-to-average' and '0-to-peak'.

rules.fork: Higgs sector: ½λ(φ†φ)² vs λ(φ†φ)²; +m² vs −μ² · C102
rules.branch: ½λ(φ†φ)²: the quartic carries an explicit ½, so m_h² = λv²
rules.rival: λ(φ†φ)² with no ½, where m_h² = 2λv² and the same m_h means half the λ
rules.meaning: The quartic is printed with a ½, so the Higgs mass is m_h² = λv² and this λ is half the one a no-½ potential reports.
rules.census: §5 round-4 empirical-pilot table, HEP/lattice/cosmology block row 'Higgs sector: ½λ(φ†φ)² vs λ(φ†φ)²; +m² vs −μ² · C102', Detection column 'the printed potential'
rules.notes: Only the quartic-normalization leg; the +m² vs −μ² sign leg of the same census row is a separate rule. λ/4 with a shifted field (the (φ†φ − v²/2)² form) is a THIRD normalization and is carried as a negative so this rule never claims it. Not tested against a real SMEFT paper.
